headline: Committee of States Estimates Future Consumption Tax on Brazilians at 28% by 2033; Rate Exceeds That of OECD Countries
summary: A Brazilian committee estimates the future consumption tax rate needed to maintain the current burden will reach 28% by 2033, above OECD averages. A bill to reduce it must go to Congress if the burden hits 26.5%.
why: Brazil's tax reform sets the rate of consumption taxes on goods and services, which affects business costs, pricing and the fiscal outlook.
